established:
MODEL (as relayed): normal play; a passer = +/-BIG (e.p.-aware test); race rules count/mover/opponent; trebuchet kings frozen = 0; sum safety.

A. Solver infrastructure (CHECKED-2). kings/kpsolve (C; --board flat|cyl:WxH, --ep, --promote QRBN, --cap C, --frozen, --moves) agrees with the independent Python kings/ref on 1,418,480 positions (3-5 files), and with atlas/cylinder/kpk on all 326,640 cylinder KPK positions (flat: only the 6 rook-underpromotion positions differ). Lichess check: 45 comparable positions, 42 exact, 3 need a second promotion (truth inside kpsolve's bounds); king groups 8/8 (kings/results/lichess_check_2-4_cap1.txt, king_groups_lichess.txt). cylcgt agrees with sumtest's independent solver on 4,967,550 outcome predictions, and on 3,600/3,600 two-component positions; whole-board differs exactly on the 100 sum_safe=False positions (sumtest/REPORT.md). Underpromotion: a 4x4 position where only a rook promotion wins is handled; on 6x6 cylinder 42/42 exact results equal queen-only.

B. Where the convention matches real chess (kings/REPORT.md, theory/LOOPY.md). Theorem 1.14(i) PROVED: with (V1)-(V3) (kings never interact, no stalemate, e.p. condition (E), every decisive event really wins, every king-group move punished) the result is the normal-play result. Prop 1.15 PROVED. Theorem 2.7 PROVED after repair only in the 'first promotion wins' model P; it does NOT give a chess win (kpsolve cap-2 counterexamples Kb4 ka1 Pe4 pa2 and Kc5 ka3 Pe2 pc4), so a chess conclusion needs a per-position check (A_Q). The 'real-king square rule' is FALSE as stated (stalemate; K16). Spare king tempo moves give loopy on/off/dud, not 0 (Theorem 3.4 PROVED, all AI referees). K12: 76,744 roots on one board, 515,780 on 7x6, 68,036 on 8x6, 0 certified disagreements (56,402 e.p. roots excluded).

C. Measured agreement, small boards (kings/REPORT.md section 4; COMPUTED-1, kpsolve queen-only, cap 2, e.p. on, 6-rank boards): sweeps of every pawn component (<=2 pawns a side) beside a trebuchet: 6x6 cyl 13/26 match, 5x6 flat 23/26, 7x6 cyl 305/448 (6 undetermined); total 341/500 = 68% match, 159 mismatch. 107 are king effects (frozen-king control equals cylcgt); 52 (all 7x6) fail even with frozen kings: 18 e.p. (fixed by e.p.-aware test), 34 'passer wins at once' failures (V2); e.p.-aware drops 7x6 mismatches 143 -> 138. Of 896 components 390 are races at start and are untestable. Per-move diagnosis exists only for 6x6/5x6 (20+3 sides); 7x6 deferred (cap-2 needs ~9 GB, above the 4 GB per-process rule).

D. Flat 8x8, Lichess 7-man + search (realchess/REPORT.md; checked two ways by an AND/OR prover): the *2 candidate W a2 c2 / B b7 d7 + trebuchet: root is N (side to move wins), matches *2 and the model; Black's only winning root move b5, White's c4, matching the model; oracle value never *2 or 0 in the e.p.-aware tree, exactly {2+-1 | -2+-1} when draws count as Black wins (both trees). Node-level: 462 textbook-tree positions, 295 resolved; 119 configs with both sides resolved; class agreement (count rule) 91/119 textbook, 92/119 e.p.-aware (mover 90/91, opponent 85/85). Per position e.p.-aware count: 268 agree, 14 disagree, plus 13 real draws (so 268/295 = 91%; excluding draws 95%); opponent rule 247/35. Typical failure: model says N, truth is L, R or draw. Terminals: L/R terminals that count gets wrong: 4 in each tree (20 under opponent); 3 draw terminals. King moves at nodes: 1431 generated, 133 proven losing, 6 proven drawing, 0 proven winning, 1292 unresolved. No cursed/blessed results appear in any record, so 50-move mode is irrelevant there. 8-man Lichess categories existed for 678/915 records and agreed with search on 201/201 nodes (used only as a cross-check).

E. Engine suite (engine/suite): 233 tablebase-checked positions; 181 cgt_verified, 52 cgt_disagree (22% CGT/tablebase disagreement). 94 tablebase-checked trebuchet positions: 41 of 449 king moves draw and 7 win. Stockfish 19 solves 232/233 at 1k nodes; Lc0 perfect at every budget.

F. Real-chess 1/8 (realchess/targets18/, C1): O = 1/8 exactly, with kpsolve queen-promotion-only, frozen kings; 302 sides of <=7 men resolved (290 one-sided: 283 agree, 5 disagree, 2 draws); 8-man: 7 agree, 1 disagrees (W a3 a5 / B b4 b5, Black wins, against the model); all 4 decisive 8-9-man end positions agree with the model; hardest (W b2 b5 / B a5 b4, Black to move) took 6.1e10 states, 15.6 h, cap 2. A rerun with underpromotions (--promote QRBN) is NOT done, so it is not yet a full-chess certificate. ups-squared-star and tiny(1): every resolved end position agrees; lower bound equals target; 10 and 12 end positions of 9-10 men still open.

G. Failure catalogue (kings/results/FAILURES.md, REPORT section 6): 7.2 king group (Ke6 Pd7 / Kd8 Pe7) is not a mutual zugzwang in real chess (White draws with Kd5/Ke5/Kf5; CHECKED-2 flat); drawing king moves exist at *2 terminals (W a5 / B b7 c5: Ke4/Ke5; W a5 c3 / B b7 d5; suite cgt055, cgt123 (all five king moves draw), cgt262, cgt270). On the 8-file cylinder the A2 FEN freeze fails (1.a3 checks Kh4 across the seam); no *k (k>=2) with <=5 pawns can be frozen on 8-file cylinder (0/40 placements; computed once). Trebuchets (5.1 cylinder, 7.1 c/f files) are real mutual zugzwangs. Z_T (T>=2) acts as 0 only beside slow/locked components (P4: both theory and convention wrong in 3 of 6 contexts; K23 shows context dependence). Direct opposition on C8x8: 984 of 4,288 triples draws, 200 mutual zugzwangs (refutes 'always draw'). K20: finite king tempo exists when the opponent is not frozen (flat 6x6 Kc3 ka4 Pa2 pa3 Pc4 pc5 = +1 in the D-model sum battery).

H. Positions A/B (11 men beside T, C3 ring *2 needing two e.p. captures): one *2 up to colour reversal+mirror; all 12 decisive 8-man end positions agree with the model; the 9-11-man end positions are unsolved, so their *2 is model-only. The 4-file candidate W a3 b3 c2 e2 / B a6 c5 d5 e3 (12 men) is open. Second flat candidate W a3 b3 c2 / B b5 b7 c6 is refuted (oracle > 0). Three other candidates have race verdicts contradicted by the tablebase.
gaps:
1. No single headline agreement rate exists: figures come from different samples (68% on 500 small-board components, 91-95% of 295 node positions of one tree, 78% on the 233-position suite, 91-92/119 configurations) with different board sizes, promotion settings and draw treatments; none is a random or exhaustive class, and no confidence intervals. Selection bias is large (components chosen for CGT interest, many races untestable: 390 of 896).
2. Model-versus-chess agreement has never been measured over a whole enumerated class on the actual cylinder with explicit kings. Real-chess evidence on the cylinder comes only from kpsolve on small boards (up to 7x6/8x6); the Lichess tablebase is flat only, and the 8x8 cylinder node tree is not tabulated (FEN freeze fails there).
3. Error attribution is only partial: the 7x6 sweep has no per-move diagnosis (cap-2 memory), 21 of 52 convention failures also have king effects, and 'passer wins at once' failures (34) are not classified by cause (stalemate, king catch-up, underpromotion, capture-the-passer, a king stepping into the queening square).
4. Race rules count/mover/opponent are each refuted by lemma L4 forced-win counterexamples, yet no corrected race rule exists. Agreement of the three rules against truth (92/91/85 of 119) is measured only on one tree; no systematic search for the smallest counterexample per convention.
5. Promotion models: most results use queen-only promotion, cap 2. Full QRBN reruns are missing for the 1/8 certificate. Underpromotion has only a 4x4 example plus 42/42 on 6x6. Cap-limited (officer cap) runs give bounds not exact values in places.
6. Draw handling: the oracle value depends on the draw treatment (draw as 0 gives an interval; 'Black must win' unpinned, 58 essential open sides); a principled loopy/affine treatment is only mentioned. 50-move rule not modelled (no cursed/blessed in data, but untested for deeper cases).
7. King effects are described but not modelled: 1292 of 1431 king moves at the 8-man nodes unresolved; 41 of 449 king moves in the suite draw and 7 win; the V3 punishment horizon T for real trebuchets is 5-7 so Z is certified 0 only beside slow components. No quantitative model of when kings leave the freeze.
8. Sum accuracy: the sum safety theorem is tested in the cylcgt-versus-brute-force sense (sum_safe flag; 100 exceptions) but not against explicit-king chess in sums on 8x8 (no room for two components). The Lichess side only validates single components; nothing real-chess validates sums beyond kpsolve on 7x6/8x6 small components.
9. Open items: White root moves a3, a4, c3; the 8-man side 8/3p4/Pp6/2P2Kp1/6Pk/8/8/8 b; position A/B 9-11-man end positions; 1/8 underpromotion rerun; e.p. roots excluded (56,402) from K12 recheck; Theorem 2.7 and the Z_T context dependence only AI-reviewed. Model-versus-engine comparison is on easy 7-man positions where engines are already perfect.

- Elkies' small values on flat boards, widths 1-4, at most 6 pawns (231,071 records, two independent solvers). E.p.-aware counts: 1/8 9, 1/16 2, 1/32 0, up-second 2, up-second-star 10, tiny(1) 16. Non-integer tiny(x) never occurs. 1/8 has a robust exemplar `W a2 a3 b2 / B a6 b5 b6`, equal to 1/8 in all 9 settings. A real-chess 1/8 has oracle value exactly 1/8 with queen promotions only and frozen kings (C1).
- Hot values: the hottest BIG-free value is +-3 (research/thermo/REPORT.md, COMPUTED-1). BIG-free atomic weights -2..2 occur and none >= 3. The mean-value check (mean of a sum equals the sum of the means) has 0 failures on more than 10^4 sums.
- Kings, K+P vs K without edges (K4, CHECKED-2): every placement is a decisive win, on, off or dud. No number or infinitesimal occurs. Gafni's on-star and {on|0} do not occur.

NIMBERS AND RINGS
- *2:
  - The textbook *2 on flat 4 files, `W a2 c2 / B b7 d7`, is an e.p. artefact. It is {2+-1 | -2+-1} under the adopted convention.
  - The first genuine *2 on flat boards has 7 pawns (positions A and B, one *2 up to colour reversal).
  - Ring minimum of pawns for a *2: n+3 for n=3..7 (CHECKED-2), 10 for n=7..10 (C2), and n for n>=10 (PROVED [S]; the lower bound n is trivial because a ring needs a pawn on every file).
  - Families: M_n / O_n with n pawns, wall families P/R with n+2 pawns, and the wall families O_n / E_n with n+3 pawns, all proved [AI] with Codex or OpenCode referees SOUND. All are whole-board results.
- *3:
  - No default-setting single-component *3 on flat boards or C3-C6 within the scopes searched.
  - First default-setting single-component *3: C7 with 10 pawns (8 rings).
  - n+1 pawns on C11..C59 (T_n / S_n, C1 to n=15).
  - Qo and Q families with n+2 pawns (Codex referee SOUND).
  - Wherever *3 appears at low pawn counts it is *2 + * (the 13 minimal flat *3 cores are each a *2 plus a *1 pair).
- *4: none.
  - 134.9M ten-pawn positions on 5 files and 48.6M eleven-pawn positions on 4 files contain none.
  - About 23.6M core-in-wall, grown and two-core rings contain none.
  - 14,090 T56 candidates and 1,280 C10 wall rings contain none.
  - Two cores separated by a wall of 7-11 files: whenever the ring is a nimber it equals the nim-sum of the two core values (1,513 of 1,890 rings, no exception). The other 377 are decisive.
- Sum safety: the HSS (hereditarily sum-safe) theorem is proved, `sum_safe()` is only a heuristic, and condition (E) on e.p. rights is needed for the sum to be exact.
- Kings and loopy values:
  - Theorem 1.14 and conditions (V1)-(V4) are proved in P, with repairs and several non-Claude re-derivations (K13, K33, K36, K37).
  - on/off/dud sum theorems T3.7/T3.8 are proved, with K33 (Codex) re-proving them.
  - P3.2' (two shuttling kings are a dud) is proved in the D-model.
  - The trebuchet zero is context-dependent (P2.10(b), CHECKED-2).
- Dawson's chess:
  - The cylinder ring rule (first player wins iff g(n-3)=0) is proved and checked for n<=22.
  - The misere ring rule is confirmed to n=100, CHECKED-2 up to 60.
  - Torus = cylinder for 3xn is proved.
gaps:
LABELS BELOW [AI]/PROVED, AND SCOPE LIMITS
1. Sum model vs whole board for ring *2/*3 families. The wall families (P, Q, R, Qo, O_n/E_n, M_n/O_n, T_n/S_n) are proved only in the whole-board game, where the passed-pawn test is global. As sums of components, the wall families are checked only to n=12, because wall captures split the ring (ring_family/REPORT.md, ring_family_proof/REPORT.md: 42 of 78 K-captures split the ring in O_17). P_10, Q_10, R_11, Qo_11, M_10, O_11 and C13/C14 rings were checked with cylcgt as sums. There is no theorem or general statement for the component-sum value, and the "poisoned move deletion" lemma is exact only in the whole-board model.
2. Pumping. Insertion isomorphism ("reduced graph of size 104..40,445 independent of n") is verified numerically to n<=60 and proved by a finite window argument [S]/[AI]. The "moves depend only on files within about 5" locality was only verified to wall length 15 (ring_family REPORT, CONJECTURE). This is the main reason the *3 families T_n/S_n are only C1 for n>15.
3. *3 minimality: whether a ring *3 can have one pawn per file is open. C11 exhaustive for 11 pawns: none. Nothing for C12+ or for C10 other than "none among the 4.3M rings in splits 4+6, 5+5".
4. *4 and higher: only a CONJECTURE that a *4 needs a new primitive of nimber 4 at 12 or more pawns. The nim-sum-of-cores argument is empirical (1,513 rings), not proved. The search has been exhaustive only for single cores of at most about 10-11 pawns on narrow boards and for walls up to 11 files.
5. Atlas completeness. Rings with 6-8 pawns on C6-C8 (the only place a wide cylinder can show new values) were never enumerated at the canonical-value level. Cylinder-only values are listed under the e.p.-aware test only up to 5 pawns, and every cylinder-only value is race-rule dependent. The atlas is COMPUTED-1 for values and CHECKED-2 only for outcomes.
6. Thermography (research/thermo/REPORT.md) is COMPUTED-1 and its method is weak: "truly BIG-free" is inferred from temperature <= 3, not from the game tree. Atomic weights for non-all-small infinitesimals use additivity from a few base cases, and the two-ahead rule is an untested CONJECTURE. No thermographs of ring values or of the *2/*3 rings are reported, and no temperature theory for loopy components.
7. Small-value targets: 1/32 does not occur at all in the flat-width<=4, <=6-pawn census once e.p. is aware. Wider boards and 7 or more pawns were not tested for 1/16, 1/32 or other dyadics. The Elkies "tiny(x), x non-integer" and "tiny(1 up-arrow)" questions are census-bounded only. Some Elkies-target census items are COMPUTED-1 under the e.p.-aware test (the table column is C1).
8. Kings and loopy values: the Gafni thesis was not located; the conjecture C4.7 is stated only for <=2+2 pawns; P4 (which the convention predicts for six contexts) is refuted by kpsolve in chess in 3 of 6 contexts, and the cause "was not examined" (LOOPY.md row P4). No loopy canonical form theory (onside/offside of kings groups) is computed. (V1)-(V4) are sufficient, not necessary. The chess-vs-P gap is characterised only by examples.
9. Dawson: misere quotient (Q33 not converged; infinite quotient conjecture), Möbius and torus equal 3xn only partially understood, 4xn and 5xn boards have no octal-game reduction ("debris"), and Möbius normal play first-player wins n=3..12 is just a computation.
10. Real-chess link for *2: A and B oracle values stay open (9-11 man end positions unsolved), a *k for k>=2 with 8x8 legal geometry and kings is still not certified, and the cylinder with 8 files cannot freeze any *k (0 of 40 placements). The 1/8 certificate is queen-promotion-only.
11. Open question 1.8 (stale e.p. rights at the root) in notes/lemmas.md, whether HSS is also necessary, and whether a multi-component sum_safe counterexample exists.
12. Known discrepancy to chase: star2_frontier/REPORT.md lines 67-71 report two positions where the C mask scan says *2 (opponent rule, e.p.-aware) and cylcgt on flat Board(5,8) returns up-arrow-type values. This was left as a COMPUTED-1 discrepancy in the report as read.

avenues.title: Prove locality (the window lemma) and make the pumping proofs uniform
avenues.question: Prove that in a ring or wall position the reduced-game moves of a pawn depend only on pawns within radius r of it (r about 5 from the data), so one lemma gives the insertion isomorphism for every n, and every currently C1 family (T_n, S_n, M_n/O_n at n>60) becomes PROVED. Then state a generic theorem: for a wall word in a finite alphabet, the value is a function of a finite-state transducer, and the ring value is eventually periodic in the wall length.
avenues.why_it_matters: Upgrades the CONJECTURE flagged in ring_family REPORT (locality verified only to wall length 15), turns six family-specific proofs into one, and makes it possible to read off new families by pure search over words. It would also give a decision procedure for the nimber of any wall ring.
avenues.first_experiment: In research/ring_family_proof run locality_test.py and pump_verify.py on every family with a wall of length L=4..30 and report the smallest L at which all of reduced-game isomorphism, node count and outcome stabilise. Then write a small stdlib script that computes, for a wall segment w, the 'behaviour' of w as the set of reduced-game transitions on its boundary pawns (distance-5 windows), and counts distinct behaviours over all words of length <=6 with alphabet from the wall families. A finite number of behaviour classes supports the transducer statement. Output: a table L -> number of distinct windows and a Myhill-Nerode class count.
avenues.existing_tools: research/ring_family_proof/{fam.py, graph.py, locality_test.py, pump_verify.py}, research/ring_n_check (Codex checker), the LaTeX proofs in research/ring_family_proof/proof.tex.
avenues.cost: Cheap computationally (minutes to an hour, under 2 GB). The proof write-up is a few agent-sessions plus a Codex or OpenCode referee run. No heavy CPU.
avenues.novelty: Partly known technique (pumping), new for this model. It would make the ring nimber theory structural rather than case-based.

avenues.title: A nim-sum / additivity theorem for separated cores and a coupling criterion
avenues.question: State and prove: if two cores are separated by a wall of at least w files on a ring, the ring value is the sum of the core values whenever both are nimbers, and decisive otherwise. Find the least w, and say exactly which cores couple (the 377 of 1,890 two-core rings that were decisive).
avenues.why_it_matters: The *4 hunt rests on 'nim-sum of cores, no exception in 1,513 rings'. If this is a theorem, then a *4 ring must contain a single primitive *4 core and the whole search space narrows to cores. The coupling rule also gives the first structural theory of how rings fail to be sums, which is a model-justification statement.
avenues.first_experiment: Use research/star4_rings/two_core/fail_scan.py and the rg binary in research/star4_rings. For all cores (A,B) of at most 6 pawns each, vary the two wall lengths L1, L2 from 3 to 14 and tabulate: nimber of ring versus vA xor vB, and for each decisive ring which core move sequence reaches a passed pawn across the wall. Output: the minimal L above which equality is exact for every pair, plus the list of coupling mechanisms (e.g. a capture that opens a file, a double-step e.p. across a wall pawn). Compare with the proved 'delete poisoned moves' lemma to see whether the coupling is exactly the poison-deletion failing.
avenues.existing_tools: research/star4_rings/two_core (rg, fail_scan.py), research/star4_hunt, cylcgt for sum-vs-whole on the failures.
avenues.cost: two_core already ran 207,975 rings. The extension (L up to 14, cores up to 6 pawns) is a few CPU-hours at 3 cores and about 1-2 GB each. One agent session to analyse the failures; the proof is a separate task.

avenues.title: Rigorous thermography and atomic weights of the census, including rings
avenues.question: Replace the 'temperature <= 3 means BIG-free' proxy with exact thermographs where BIG is a parameter N, and report which values are stable as N grows. What are the temperature and mean of each ring *2/*3 and of the hot cylinder-only values, and is the two-ahead rule true?
avenues.why_it_matters: Thermography is the standard tool for 'when does the sum model predict the winning move' (Principle 2 of 05_sums). The current thermo REPORT is COMPUTED-1 with a heuristic filter and an untested rule, so it cannot support claims about the temperature ceiling (3) or the atomic weights (max 2). A rigorous version would turn a section of the paper from a pilot to a result, and would explain Stockfish's failure on infinitesimals via exact temperatures.

SLICE: boards/variants/tablebases/Dawson/engines/learning. Labels follow the repo (COMPUTED-1 = one program, CHECKED-2 = two independent programs, PROVED, CONJECTURE).

TABLEBASES (paper s10; tablebase/replica/REPORT.md, tablebase/egt_prototype.c). 24 pawnless 4-man tables (KQK, KRK, KBBK opp-colour, KBNK, KNNK, KRBK, KRRK, KQRK on flat/cylinder/torus), about 607M values, two independent solvers (replica.c, egt_prototype.c) agree plus Bellman and symmetry self-checks. CHECKED-2. Headline: cylinder KRK won 2.80%, KBNK 0.0245%, KBBK(opp) 100%; torus only KRRK and KQRK win everywhere. KPK on 8x8 cylinder/flat: all 326,640 cylinder positions agree between two solvers (kings/kpsolve all promotions vs a queen-only solver); n=3..8 widths agree between two solvers; 216 mutual zugzwangs on cyl vs 160 flat. CHECKED-2. KPKP: about 89% of legal cylinder positions decided (kings/ solver, one extra promoted piece); KPPK open (research/kpkp/, compressed .zst files).

MOBIUS/KLEIN (research/mobius/REPORT.md, REPORT_T35.md, RULES.md; research/twisted_tablebases/COMPARE.md). KRK is won from every legal Mobius position (147,776 positions, mate <= 12) and RP2 (124,848) and only 960/145,344 (0.66%) on the Klein bottle: CHECKED-2, independent of the ray rule. KPK on 8x8 Mobius: White-to-move wins 126,816/160,656 = 78.94% (cyl 78.89%); Ka6 Pa5 v Ka8 won both sides to move on Mobius and cylinder; 216 mutual zugzwangs; CHECKED-2 (patched kpsolve_mob vs ref_mob_solve.py). Mobius pawn game (mob_pawns.py, fork of cylcgt with seam flip and direction flag): 2,419 (w3) / 3,018 (w4) distinct values, 1,190 / 1,286 values on neither cylinder nor flat; COMPUTED-1 plus verifier recomputation. T9's own Part B (1,659/2,342 'unique' values) does not model the seam (no 9-r flip; passed/e.p. tests ignore it) and is invalid. Bishop/queen results on twisted boards depend on the slider-ray rule (A's rule keeps local direction and lets a lone bishop win KBK; B's straight-ray rule reflects at the seam); there is no 2-colouring of squares, so 'opposite-colour bishops' does not exist. Only the rook results are paper-grade.

DAWSON (paper s11; dawson/REPORT.md). Rules of 3xn Dawson's chess = octal 0.137, g(n) period 34, last exception n=51 (classical). Ring rule: cylinder first move leaves one strip of n-3 files (PROVED, machine-checked n<=16 in report, n<=22 in paper); the 2025 paper's recurrence agrees with g on only 31/301 values and gets 56 cylinder outcomes wrong (two implementations). Misere: exhaustive search over all 359,799,167 sums of strips total <=100 (Python=C to total 60, C only above); my reimplementation of Plambeck-Siegel reproduces the published quotient for strips <=32 (order 638, 109 P-portion), agrees with exhaustive search on 7.4M positions; the strip <=33 quotient did not converge (candidate orders 1580, 1922, 5236, 6740, 18408 in 28 min at load ~128). No period visible in misere single-strip outcomes to 100; infinite quotient is only a conjecture. dawson_variants/REPORT.md: misere ring rule PROVED; torus = cylinder PROVED; Mobius 3xn Dawson with colour flip does not reduce to an octal game (debris), COMPUTED-1 n<=12; 4xn and 5xn flat/cylinder: no clean strip decomposition, COMPUTED-1 small n only.

ENGINES (paper s12; engine/README.md, ENGINES.md, FAIRY_CYLINDER.md). 233-position <=7-man CGT suite, tablebase-checked (181 agree with CGT, 52 disagree). Stockfish 19 solves 232/233 at 1,000 nodes; Lc0 233/233 at 1,000 nodes. Depth 1: infinitesimals 30% and nimbers 53% correct vs hot 81% (single engine, pilot). Static NNUE eval right for 96% of CGT-number positions but 25% of nimber positions (4/16); Lc0 value head 88% (14/16); null-move and Step-15 pruning inert in K+P until promotion; reverse futility is the zugzwang-relevant cut. ChessSums: 26,000 sums, 418 components, 37 distinct values; whole-board alpha-beta confirms all but 5 (time limits), minimax confirms 4,887 (CHECKED-2); alpha-beta costs 4-9x nodes per added component. Engines on 15-20 man sums (200 positions): Stockfish picks a winning move only 26.5-28% and Lc0 32.5-33.5%, but the ground truth is the frozen-king model, so this measures agreement with the model, not real-chess error. FAIRY_CYLINDER.md is a design for a cylinder engine (bitboard wrap, NNUE features, perft plan); engine/perft has two reference cylinder move generators (C and Python) with perft to depth 6 for the start position.

LEARNING. ml/dawson: LSTM trained on total length <=30 gets 0.82 on lengths 31-80 vs 0.79 majority, linear probes no better than majority; rule scores 1.0; MLP/DeepSets also fail (COMPUTED-1). ml/chesssums_baseline: MLP/CNN/transformer baselines on ChessSums get low accuracy (MLP test 0.446 overall, 0.63 on held-out split; need the REPORT for the others). Zhou and Riis showed AlphaZero fails Nim parity (literature, per RESEARCH_PLAN).

HIGHER NIMBERS (outside slice but touches 'rank counts'): ring *2 minimum pawn counts and *3 families are established elsewhere (RESULTS.md 6c); no *4 found in about 23.6M rings; cylcgt Board has a ranks parameter (default 8), so rank counts above 8 appear supported by the engine but no reported run uses them.
gaps: 1) T9 Part A tablebase counts are unverified: kpsolve_mob.c (line 95) and mobius_replica.c (line 102) declare ray arrays [64][8][8] but Mobius/Klein horizontal rays have 15 squares, out-of-bounds writes (UBSan-confirmed). Legal counts change (KQK 98,956 not 99,013; KRK 147,776 not 148,171). Win rates and DTMs are unchanged in the tables the verifier re-ran (Q, R, B, BB), but the Klein tables and the other materials were not re-run. 2) Bishop/queen results on twisted boards are tied to a ray convention (A's non-geometric one vs B's straight-ray one, only B COMPUTED-1). Bishop 'colour' is undefined on twisted boards. 3) No 5-man (let alone 6-man) pawnless table exists for cylinder/torus/Mobius; no KQKR, KRKB, KQKP, KRKP cylinder analogues (Philidor, Lucena); KPPK on the cylinder and KPKP with several promotions are open (paper conclusion item 5). No DTM/DTZ for pawn endings on the cylinder; no 50-move rule. 4) Mobius pawn game: the 1,190/1,286 'new value' counts are dominated by the BIG stand-in (1,162/1,252 contain W; only 28/34 are BIG-free), about 30-38% of positions are excluded because both sides have passers, seam conventions (double-step home rank, passed-pawn test across the flip) are the agent's own extensions and untested against alternatives, and it is unproven that the sum safety theorem (independent components add) survives non-orientable files. Mobius KPK is CHECKED-2 but the pawn spectrum is only COMPUTED-1. The Mobius or Klein versions of the real-chess certification (kings/kpsolve vs the model) were not run. Torus pawns: ranks wrap, so pawns have no promotion rank; not even defined in the repo for the pawn game. 5) Dawson: misere quotient for strips >=33 unsolved; misere outcomes for totals 61..100 are one program only; Mobius/4xn/5xn variants exist only for small n and have no structural theory; no run for other octal/pawn games (e.g. with a double step, or ranks >3) or for partizan Dawson. Misere cylinder claims for 61<=n<=100 are COMPUTED-1. 6) Engines: the suite is too easy; the single-engine pilot on 233 positions is not strong evidence; Stockfish classes in Table 12 have small n (17 nimbers). The 15-20 man sum experiment is measured against the frozen-king model, not real chess. P2, P8, P9, P10, L2, L3 of the ENGINES scorecard are untested (nodes-to-solve vs number of components E4, Syzygy effect E7, frozen-king false NMP E8). No evaluation of Fairy-Stockfish on the cylinder; no cylinder NNUE or fixed-point test of cylinder perft beyond depth 6; the Lc0 policy accuracy on k-component nimber sums (L2) is untested. 7) Learning: LSTM on Dawson only reached the majority-class level; no experiment gave the network the Grundy values of strips, no architecture with an XOR inductive bias (Deep Sets with Z2^m latent, planned C2 in RESEARCH_PLAN) has been finished; no AlphaZero/self-play run (planned C3); nothing on learning CGT values of cylinder pawn components; ChessSums neural baselines report a modest accuracy and have no scaling-in-k study with a circular-padded (cyclically equivariant) CNN. The 'RL-trained LLM' ideas in the plan are not started. 8) No run uses rank counts other than 8 in the pawn game (cylcgt supports ranks); *4, and ring *3 with one pawn per file, are open at 8 ranks; whether 9+ ranks gives new nimbers is unknown. Also unknown: whether the Mobius file twist on a pawn game can make a ring *k with fewer pawns.

avenues.title: A. Repair and extend the twisted-board tablebases, with ray rule as a variable
avenues.question: What are the correct 4-man (and first 5-man) results on Mobius, Klein and RP2 once the ray-array overflow is fixed, and which bishop/queen/KBNK claims survive under the geometric straight-ray rule versus A's local-direction rule?
avenues.why_it_matters: The Mobius/Klein tablebase is the paper's most exotic result and the only one the T35 verifier showed was computed on corrupted arrays; it currently supports only rook claims. Fixing it gives a clean result, shows which pieces' mating power is topological (rook, knight) and which depend on convention (bishop, queen), and is what open problem 5 of the paper rests on.
avenues.first_experiment: In research/mobius/ copy mobius_replica.c and kpsolve_mob.c, change the rayL / rayBefore arrays from [64][8][8] to [64][8][16] (the verifier said 15 squares suffice), compile with -fsanitize=undefined, and re-run all 9 materials on Mobius, Klein and the RP2 variant. Run once with the repo rule (rays reflect at the seam, matching RULES.md section 5) and once with the straight-ray rule in twisted_tablebases/B. Command sketch: cc -O2 -fsanitize=undefined -pthread mobius_replica.c -o mr_fixed; for m in Q R BB B BN NN RB RR QR; do ./mr_fixed mobius $m; ./mr_fixed klein $m; done. Compare against twisted_tablebases/A and B result dirs with a short diff script on legal count, won count and max DTM. Success: UBSan silent, KQK 98,956 legal, win rates and DTMs matching the verifier's, and a table showing which rows differ by ray rule. Then add KQKR or KRKB 5-man pawnless on the cylinder as a smoke test (see avenue C).
avenues.existing_tools: research/mobius/mobius_replica.c, kpsolve_mob.c; research/twisted_tablebases/A and B; tablebase/replica/replica.c as the flat/cylinder/torus control; UBSan from clang.
avenues.cost: Each 4-man table is minutes on 14 threads, KBNK/KNNK the largest (10M legal positions); total well under an hour and under 2 GB RAM. Low agent effort (one small patch plus a diff script).

avenues.title: B. Mobius pawn atlas: BIG-free values, a ring *k on the twisted ring, and a sum-safety test
avenues.question: On the Mobius strip, do independent pawn components still add (the sum safety theorem), do BIG-free new values (numbers, nimbers, ups) exist beyond the 28/34 the verifier found, and is there a *2 or *3 with fewer pawns than on the cylinder ring?
avenues.why_it_matters: Every piece of the model (BIG, e.p., trebuchet, sums) assumes a locally oriented board. The Mobius strip is the first topology where a pawn can reverse direction, so it tests exactly where the model breaks. A twisted ring *2 with fewer than n+3 pawns would be a new topological phenomenon, and a failure of additivity would be a theorem-level result for the paper's limitations section.
avenues.first_experiment: Use research/mobius/mob_pawns.py (the corrected fork). (1) Sum test: take 3000 random pairs of BIG-free Mobius components from pawn_w3_p4c_unique.tsv and its flat neighbours, form the disjoint union on width 6 using wide-flat placement (not touching the seam) and also pairs where one component sits on the seam, evaluate the whole board by a direct alpha-beta in mob_pawns.py, and compare with the sum of the cylcgt canonical values. Report mismatch rate for seam-touching versus not. (2) Convention test: rerun pawn_values_mobius.py for width 3, 4 pawns with the double-step home rank fixed by colour (the verifier already did: 2,423 distinct, 1,194 unique) and with two alternative passed-pawn tests (ignore flipped enemy pawns; treat flipped pawn as passed only if it cannot be captured); record which BIG-free unique values survive in all variants. (3) Ring scan: for Mobius width 4 and 5, enumerate all 6- to 8-pawn positions modulo the symmetry in check_mob_symmetry.py, keep those with value *2 or *3, and compare the minimum pawn count with cylinder C4/C5 (n+3 for *2).
avenues.existing_tools: research/mobius/mob_pawns.py, pawn_values_mobius.py, check_mob_symmetry.py, check_mob_pawns.py; cylcgt.cgt canonical forms; research/ring_family and ring_n_check scripts for the ring enumeration; no external tool handles a twisted pawn game.
avenues.cost: Width 3-4 enumeration took minutes to an hour in earlier runs (187k to 617k canonical positions). The ring scan to 8 pawns on width 5 is of order 10^6 to 10^7 positions, a few CPU-hours in Python, so run it under taskset-free nice -n 19 on 4 cores. Medium agent effort; keep a second independent implementation (Codex) for the ring scan since only the single fork exists.

avenues.title: C. Five-man pawnless cylinder tablebases and the cylinder Lucena/Philidor question
avenues.question: Does KQKR, KRKB, KRKN, KQKB or KBBKN become a draw/win on the cylinder where it is on the flat board, and are there cylinder analogues of the Lucena and Philidor positions?
avenues.why_it_matters: The paper's tablebase section stops at 4 men and KPK. Practical endgames need 5-man data, and the cylinder lacks corners and edges so classical fortresses and mating nets must change. This also gives engine ground truth beyond 4 men for avenue F, and cylinder KPPK/KRKP would extend open problem 5 (KPPK).
avenues.first_experiment: Take tablebase/replica/replica.c (already generalised over wrap flags, 14 threads, Bellman and symmetry self-checks) and add 5-man index support for KQKR first (64^5 = 1.07e9 squares combinations, two sides to move, 1 byte per position about 2 GB). Run on cylinder only, with the file-shift symmetry to cut work 8x (positions canonicalised by shifting the white king to file a). Output won/drawn/lost shares and longest DTM, compare to the flat Syzygy numbers (KQKR is 'about 100% win for the queen with the right side'; Lichess API confirms individual flat positions at 5 men only if you ask the user first for bulk traffic). Self-check: Bellman equations on the whole table, plus run the same code on flat boards and compare with the published longest KQKR mate (DTM 35 in the literature). Then rerun for KRKB, KRKN.
avenues.existing_tools: tablebase/replica/replica.c, tablebase/egt_prototype.c as the independent cross-check; Syzygy via the Lichess API (7-man only; user OK needed for bulk traffic).
avenues.cost: A 5-man table is about 1e9 positions with 14 threads; the 4-man ones took minutes, so expect 1-3 hours per material and 2-4 GB RAM (stay under 8 GB because the machine is shared). Compress the output (CLAUDE note: disk filled on 2026-10-22). Medium agent effort, one needs care in the symmetry reduction; do the independent re-implementation via Codex from the rules only.

avenues.title: D. Torus pawns, ranks beyond 8, and the n-by-r nimber atlas
avenues.question: Does adding ranks (9, 10, 12) produce new nimbers (the first *4, or a one-pawn-per-file ring *3), and what is a pawn game on a torus (ranks wrap) where there is no promotion rank?
avenues.why_it_matters: Open problem 3 asks whether *4 exists on eight ranks, and nothing has been run with a different rank count even though cylcgt's Board has a ranks parameter. More ranks means longer pawn runs and larger delays, the natural place for higher nimbers. A torus pawn game (which this paper does not define at all) is the missing fifth board in the pawn section and tests whether BIG stays meaningful when no pawn can promote.
avenues.first_experiment: (1) Ranks: run the existing minimum-pawn ring search for *2 and *3 (research/ring_min_c5c6, ring_n_check) on C3 to C6 with Board(ranks=9) and Board(ranks=10), 4 to 9 pawns, and tabulate the minimum pawn count and the number of *2/*3 rings for ranks 8, 9, 10, comparing the n+3 rule. Check the passed-pawn and double-step definitions at the new ranks (home ranks 2 and ranks-1). (2) Torus: in a copy of cylcgt/pawns.py add rank wrap (a white pawn on rank 8 moves to rank 1 and keeps its colour), with no promotion, so passed pawns can never be decided by promotion; define the terminal value as normal-play only (no BIG) and first compute values for 1 to 2 pawns per side on widths 3 and 4. Report whether every component is a loopy game (rank wrap makes pawn motion cyclic), which would need the loopy-game machinery.
avenues.existing_tools: cylcgt/pawns.py and cgt.py (ranks parameter exists), the ring solver rg and the ring_n_check scripts; the e.p.-aware passed test must be updated for ranks != 8.
avenues.cost: Ranks sweep is Python/Rust CPU only. Ring scans at 9 pawns on C6 were hours at 8 ranks; use width 4 and 5 first (minutes) and limit to 6 to 8 pawns; run under nice -n 19 with 4 workers. Torus pawn game needs a new loopy-game semantics, so higher agent effort and it is a design question to check in with the user about.

avenues.title: E. Misere Dawson's chess: genus sequence, wildness certificate and the Q33 quotient
avenues.question: Is the misere quotient of Dawson's chess (Dawson's Kayles 0.07, 0.137) infinite, and is the misere outcome sequence of single strips eventually periodic?
avenues.why_it_matters: Dawson's 1935 question was misere, the conclusion lists it as open problem 6, and by the ring rule any answer for strips also solves the cylinder. Plambeck and Siegel conjectured wildness; a rigorous certificate would be a genuine mathematical result, and cheaper partial evidence (genus periodicity, small-quotient failure) is a good second-tier outcome.
avenues.first_experiment: Do not just re-run the 28-minute Q33 job at load 128. (1) Compute the misere genus sequence (Conway) of 0.137/0.07 strips to n=500 with a new 80-line script from the nim-value recursion plus the genus rules (compute for each heap the sequence g_0,g_1,... the 'genus' of Conway, using misere P-ness of one and two heap-sums with a small nim-heap *2 equivalent). Check for periodicity, then compare the genus outcome against dawson/misere_c_100.txt for n up to 100 as a consistency test. (2) Run dawson/quotient.py again for Q33 under 'nice -n 19' with a wall-clock limit of 8 hours, but only after loading the machine check ('uptime'; wait until load < 8). (3) Add a cheap indistinguishability test: for the 638-element Q32, enumerate the next quotient candidate classes by 'tame' test (Plambeck's rule that a heap is tame if its misere nim-value equals its normal one in context); the first heap size where tameness fails gives a lower bound on the quotient. Output the first 40 misere P-strips beyond 100 (extend dawson/misere.c to total length 70 on all-sums or single-strips to length 400, single-strip search only) and test for a period p <= 200.
avenues.existing_tools: dawson/misere.c, misere.py, quotient.py, quotient_Q*.pkl (the saved quotients), Plambeck's MisereSolver (not installed; the repo's own re-implementation matches it for <=32), compare_misere.py.
avenues.cost: Genus script and strip-outcome extension are seconds to minutes. Q33 is the expensive part: the previous attempt had candidate orders of 18,408 when it timed out, and the memory grows quadratically, so cap at 16 GB. Run overnight on 1 core only. High payoff but low probability of a decisive answer.

avenues.title: F. Dawson on more ranks, more surfaces and with new rules: when does the octal reduction survive?
avenues.question: On 4xn and 5xn boards, on the Mobius strip, and with variants (double step, en passant, non-compulsory captures), is the game still a sum of a few component types with a periodic nim-sequence, and what is the correct octal or partizan code?
avenues.why_it_matters: The paper has only the 3xn story. dawson_variants/REPORT.md has small-n outcomes without any structure; a clean decomposition on 4xn would give a family of new octal-like games with periodicity tests, and a failure would show exactly where Dawson's reduction rests on the single row of rank-2 forced captures. Also tests whether the 'torus = cylinder' and 'Mobius is not an octal game' statements are robust.
avenues.first_experiment: In research/dawson_variants/ use solve_wider.py to enumerate, for 4xn flat n=1..14, every position reachable from the start, and group positions into 'debris types' (maximal untouched-file runs with a given boundary gap pattern). Compute for each run-type a Grundy value from the direct solver and check whether the whole-board value is the XOR of run values (sum test) over all reachable positions; the report in dawson_variants says the macro-move leaves 'gap-blocked' debris, so the key output is the finite set of debris types and their interaction table. If the types are finite, write the induced octal-like code and test period via the Guy-Smith periodicity bound. Run the identical test for 5xn and for 3xn with a double-step allowed in a 4-rank board. Compare with the Mobius n<=12 data.
avenues.existing_tools: research/dawson_variants/solve_wider.py, solve_variants.py, variants.c; cylcgt/dawson.py (ordinary 3xn solver) and dawson/octal.py for the periodicity check.
avenues.cost: Direct game-tree solving with transposition tables to n=14 on 4xn is a few minutes per board; 5xn is larger, but cap at n=12. Memory 1 to 4 GB. Low to medium agent effort.

avenues.title: G. Engine evaluation versus CGT value: dose-response and the Fairy-Stockfish cylinder engine
avenues.question: Does an engine's evaluation error grow with the number of components and with the nimber/infinitesimal content of the sum, when ground truth is the exact CGT value of the sum, and can a cylinder-native engine be tested against cylinder tablebases?
avenues.why_it_matters: Section 12 reports only agreement with the frozen-king model on 15-20 man positions and a 233-position suite that is too easy; ENGINES scorecard has P10, L2 and L3 untested. A scaling curve (nodes to solve, or accuracy versus k) with real-chess-valid positions would be the first real CGT-versus-search contrast. A Fairy-Stockfish cylinder build (FAIRY_CYLINDER.md design) would let engines play the board the tablebases cover.
avenues.first_experiment: Use the ChessSums v2 data (engine/runs/chesssums/, bench/) and the already built Stockfish 19 and Lc0. Pick positions with k = 1..6 components with all-nimber content (from the 17 nimber components and from the 5 *2/*3 components) versus all-number content, balanced by value class, 40 per cell; place each beside T on an 8x8 board with real kings, verify tablebase-free by whole-board alpha-beta (bench/ab), and run Stockfish (Threads=1, Hash=64) at fixed nodes 1e4, 1e5, 1e6 and Lc0 at 1e3, 1e4, 1e5 nodes, measuring (a) does the PV's first move belong to the winning set, (b) the signed eval for the side to move versus the CGT outcome, (c) nodes to the first correct iteration. Fit a log-linear model of nodes-to-solve vs k per class (E4 of ENGINES.md). Confirm the resulting figure with a second seed. Separately, add a small cylinder move generator test: engine/perft has the references, write a UCI wrapper for them in 100 lines and test Fairy-Stockfish variant loading (check whether it accepts the variant-ini 'cylindrical' option from FAIRY_CYLINDER.md section 1.2; if Fairy-Stockfish is not installed, stop and ask).
avenues.existing_tools: engine/run_suite.py, ablation builds in engine/vendor, Stockfish 19, Lc0 0.32.1, bench/ab, ChessSums library of 418 components, engine/perft reference movegens.
avenues.cost: 1e6 nodes per position at one thread is about 1 s per position, so 2,000 positions per engine is under one hour on 4 cores. Lc0 costs more (CPU network) so cap its budget at 1e5. Machine is loaded, so limit to 4 concurrent engines. Medium agent effort. No Syzygy for either engine.

avenues.title: H. Learning CGT values: Z2^m inductive bias, compositional generalisation and ChessSums scaling
avenues.question: Can a network learn the algebra of sums if it is given a structure-aware architecture (Deep Sets with a Z2^m latent for nimbers and a rational part for numbers, or a circular-padded CNN equivariant to file shifts), and how does accuracy generalise from k<=2 components to k=3..8?
avenues.why_it_matters: The paper's pilot (LSTM 0.82 vs 0.79 majority on Dawson sums) is a negative result with no variation in architecture; the plan (RESEARCH_PLAN C2/C3) promised compositional tests and an AlphaZero study that never ran. A positive result with a structured latent would show that the XOR rule is learnable once it is built into the model, and a failure would make a stronger negative claim than 'LSTM fails'.
avenues.first_experiment: With the existing ml/dawson data generator (gen_data.py, env.py), regenerate train sets by total length <= 30 and, as the supervised target, give the network the Grundy value of each strip (a 0..7 label; g(n) from cylcgt/dawson.py). (1) Per-strip model: a small MLP or transformer that predicts g(n) from the pile length, train n<=60 and test n=61..300 (shows period-34 extrapolation). (2) Set model: DeepSets where the aggregator is a learned map into Z2^3 realised as three sigmoid bits combined by XOR (soft XOR via the product of 1-2p), train on k<=3 strips and test on k=4..10 strips. Report outcome accuracy against the majority baseline, by k, and the probe of the per-strip embedding against g(n). Use PyTorch on MPS in the .venv-ml; keep the model under 1M parameters and training under 10 minutes. For ChessSums (ml/chesssums_baseline) add a circular-padded CNN and run the k=1..3 train, k=4..6 test split that baseline/train.py already supports through the test_by_k keys.
avenues.existing_tools: ml/dawson/{gen_data,env,model,train,eval,probe}.py, ml/chesssums_baseline/train.py, results.json (MLP, CNN, transformer), the .venv-ml virtual environment, PyTorch with MPS.
avenues.cost: Training a small net on CPU or MPS takes minutes; datasets are small (tens of thousands of positions). Whole experiment under 2 hours of wall time, one GPU-free core suffices. Low agent effort; the main care is a held-out split by total length and by number of components, and a test that the exact rule scores 1.0 on the same split.

avenues.title: A. Cut-and-glue tables for misere Dawson's chess on strips and rings
avenues.question: Is the misere quotient of Dawson's chess (octal 0.137, equivalent to Dawson's Kayles shifted by one) infinite, or can a finite quotient be found by stronger computation? The ring rule (3xn cylinder = 3x(n-3) strip) turns any answer for strips into one for the cylinder.
avenues.why_it_matters: Misere Dawson's chess is Dawson's own 1935 question and is still open. A 2007 talk abstract still lists it as unsolved after 70+ years. notes/novelty_check/REPORT.md says 'solved via Plambeck-Siegel', which is WRONG and should be fixed. Plambeck-Siegel (arXiv math/0609825) solved other octal games, not this one. Even a partial result, such as the quotient order up to n=40 or the first few indecomposable generators, would be publishable. A cylinder/ring corollary would be new on its own.
avenues.first_experiment: Rebuild the misere quotient of 0.137 incrementally with a Plambeck-Siegel style reduction: compute the equivalence classes of heap sizes 0..N by testing the outcome of all sums of up to 3 heaps drawn from heaps <= N, and check whether new classes keep appearing. Run it in Python (stdlib) or C with N = 20, 30, 40. Start from the earlier unfinished run (notes/dawson_small.txt, research/dawson_variants/dawson_variants.py). Compare against a reference: the misere 0.07 (Dawson's Kayles) quotient is known to be finite, so run it first as a sanity check. Report the number of distinct quotient elements at each N. If the count plateaus, certify it by closing the multiplication table. If it keeps growing, the growth rate is itself evidence of an infinite quotient.
avenues.existing_tools: Plambeck's MisereGameAnalysis (the 'MisereQuotients' program) and the CGSuite misere module; Siegel's Combinatorial Game Theory book, chapter on misere quotients; arXiv math/0609825 and math/0603027 (Advances in Losing).
avenues.cost: Hours of CPU for N<=30 with a pruned search. Quotient closure is exponential in the number of generators, so cap it at about 4 GB and run it single-threaded in the background. Needs an experienced agent for the algorithm (about 1 day of agent effort).
avenues.novelty: High. Open for 90 years and the cylinder link is new.

avenues.title: B. Ground-truth chess-sums benchmark: engine and neural accuracy as a function of the number of star components
avenues.question: Does Stockfish or Lc0 accuracy on tablebase-or-CGT-certified chess positions fall with the number k of nimber (star) components but not with integer components? Do engines fail on parity in the Zhou-Riis sense?
avenues.why_it_matters: The gap is documented in notes/lit_ml.md. No benchmark exists with certified CGT sum structure and a scaling study over k. The closest priors are Zhou and Riis (arXiv 2205.12787, AlphaZero fails at parity in Nim from 6-7 heaps) and Husna and Mueller (CG 2024, KataGo on Go endgames with CGT ground truth; the number of components was not varied). The repo already has a partial first pass (engine/runs/chesssums/), so this would extend rather than start from scratch.
avenues.first_experiment: Take the 10k position set already in engine/runs/chesssums/ (chesssums.epd, subset_ids.json) and its Stockfish and Lc0 outputs. Stratify by k = number of star components and by the number of integer components. For each stratum, compute the fraction of positions where the engine's best move is in the model's set of winning moves, then fit accuracy against k with logistic regression. Then add a control set where the star components are replaced by numbers of the same size, so only the nimber part differs. Expected output: one table of accuracy vs k and vs component type, plus the parity gap with a bootstrap p-value. Use fixed depth 12/16/20 for Stockfish and fixed 800 nodes for Lc0.
avenues.existing_tools: Stockfish 19, Lc0 0.32.1 (Metal backend), the cylcgt sum tester, Python stdlib. For comparison: Husna and Mueller (https://link.springer.com/ chapter in LNCS 15550), Zhou and Riis arXiv 2205.12787.
avenues.cost: A few CPU-hours for a 10k subset at fixed node counts (Stockfish depth 20 is about 0.5 s per position). Light agent effort, since the harness and data exist.
avenues.novelty: High for chess. No chess-sums benchmark exists.

avenues.title: C. Certify the 1/8 and the seven-pawn star-2 with all four promotions using the Lichess 8-man Op1 tablebase
avenues.question: Conclusion open problems 1 and 2: do the decisive 8-man end positions keep their results when under-promotions are allowed, and are positions A and B really *2 in real chess? The Lichess Op1 8-man table (positions with at least one opposing pawn pair) is now online, so the 8-man leaves can be probed directly instead of with our own solver.
avenues.why_it_matters: A certified 1/8 and a *2 in real chess would be the headline result, because Elkies left both open. Using a third-party tablebase gives an independent check that does not share our solver's code. Op1 launched in Feb 2026 (63 TiB, API available).
avenues.first_experiment: List the 8-man leaf positions of the 1/8 oracle tree (from the realchess/targets18 run that produced the 'exactly 1/8' result). Filter to those that are 8 men with an opposing pawn pair (the Op1 coverage condition). Query a single position first at https://lichess.org/api/tablebase/standard or the 8-man endpoint described in the Lichess blog, compare its WDL with the kpsolve label, and only then ask the user for permission before any bulk run (the Lichess API is rate-limited and bulk traffic needs the user's OK). The comparison table would be: kpsolve result, Op1 result, agree/disagree, for 50 hand-picked leaves first.
avenues.existing_tools: kings/kpsolve (queen-promotion-only vs all four promotions switch), Lichess tablebase API (https://lichess.org/@/Lichess/blog/op1-partial-8-piece-tablebase-available/1ptPBDpC), local Syzygy 6-man files if downloaded. Caveat: Op1 covers the flat board only, so the cylinder results cannot be checked this way. Use it only for flat-board 8x8 claims.
avenues.cost: A few hundred API calls for the first pass at roughly 1 request per second. Needs the user's OK beyond that. Alternatively download only the needed slices (82.5 GB RAM for the slice approach, per the TalkChess post), which is expensive.
avenues.novelty: High if a flat-board *2 or 1/8 is certified.

avenues.title: D. Edge-removal audit: re-derive Elkies' board-edge constructions on cyclic words and odd circumference
avenues.question: Elkies' stopped-file recursion for nimbers (*2 at file length 4, *4/*8/*16 at lengths 9/20/43) was built on a board with edges. What are the values on cyclic words, and does odd circumference (which breaks opposition parity) give new values?
avenues.why_it_matters: Listed as the top ranked opportunity in notes/lit_cgt_chess.md. Elkies' pawn game on cyclic words has never been studied. It builds on Elkies 2002 (arXiv math/0011253) and the Nowakowski open-problem list (does every *k occur, density of *k, closed form for epsilon(w)?). The current paper already has rings giving *2 with n pawns for n>=10 and *3 with n+1 pawns from n=11, so the next question is how the minimum pawn counts and the Grundy sequence look on cyclic words.
avenues.first_experiment: Take the cylcgt engine's 3-row Elkies pawns game (no double step, optional captures, reach far row wins) and run it on cyclic words of length 5..20 over the alphabet of file contents, computing the Grundy value for every word up to rotation. Compare with the linear-word table from Elkies 2002 (period 10 for the quiescent component [m] = *epsilon(m)). Expected output: a table of Grundy values by circumference n and by number of blocked files, and a check of whether 'cyclic Grundy of w' equals 'linear Grundy of w minus the seam', which would be a ring-rule analog of the Dawson result.
avenues.existing_tools: cylcgt (already handles rings), Elkies 2002 recursion, OEIS A002187 for the Dawson sequence as a test. Possibly CGSuite for cross-checking canonical forms of small cases.
avenues.cost: Cheap. A 3-row game on 20 files has at most 4^20 states, but with symmetry reduction and memoisation it needs under 8 GB. Run on 2-3 cores for a few hours.
avenues.novelty: High. Never studied, and a ring-rule theorem like the Dawson one would be a natural second paper.

avenues.title: E. Counterexample hunt for tempo and trebuchet-zero locality, and a local test for 'trebuchet is zero in chess'
avenues.question: Open problem 4 in the conclusion: find a local test (or settle Conjecture horizon2) for when a frozen trebuchet is truly 0 in chess, given that real trebuchets seem to have horizon h of about 5 to 7.
avenues.why_it_matters: This is the bridge between the model and real chess. Maeser (MGONC 2002) already warned that treating the king mutual zugzwang as permanent is heuristic. Entailing-move theory (Larsson-Nowakowski-Santos, Integers 21B 2021; Affine Normal Play, GONC6, MSRI 71, 2025) gives a possible formal frame, because a check forces a reply. A proven local criterion with a tablebase-validated failure rate would be the central 'justify the model' theorem.
avenues.first_experiment: Run the kings/kpsolve exact solver on a random sample of 2,000 trebuchet positions (kings mutually in zugzwang, a single pawn pair frozen) on the 6x6, 7x6 and 8x8 cylinders. For each, record (i) model value 0, (ii) true chess result with real kings, (iii) the king-distance horizon h at which the first deviation occurs. Fit the failure rate against distance-to-nearest-free-pawn and number of reserve tempi. Expected output: a scatter of failures with the minimal counterexample per h, which either supports the h about 5-7 conjecture or gives a smaller counterexample to feed to the referee agents.
avenues.existing_tools: kpsolve, cylcgt, the existing V1-V4 test scripts under kings/delegate/out. Theory: Larsson-Nowakowski-Santos on entailing moves; see https://projecteuclid.org or the MSRI GONC6 volume for the affine normal-play chapter.
avenues.cost: Moderate. The solver on 7x6 cylinder with promotions is the heavy part. Use a 2-4 core cap because the machine is shared. Needs a few hours.
avenues.novelty: High and central to the user's stated goal.

avenues.title: F. Hunt for infinitesimals still open from Elkies 1996: up-squared, up-star-squared, tiny-1/2 and 1/8 on the cylinder
avenues.question: Do the Elkies open values (1/8, double-up squared, tiny-x for x = 1/2 or 1 up) occur on cylinder boards with fewer men than on 8x8? Notes already record 1/8 and up-second-star as occurring in 10-man positions with legal pawn history, and Tiny 1 (C1).
avenues.why_it_matters: The paper already reports 1/8 and tiny-1 on the cylinder. Extending to ups-squared and tiny-1/2 would make the 'atlas' complete against the Elkies 1996 open list. These values are small canonical-form questions, so the CGT engine can decide them exactly. They are also the objects most sensitive to the e.p.-aware passed-pawn test.
avenues.first_experiment: Run the existing atlas search (cylcgt) over all cylinder boards C3..C7 with up to 8 pawns, and for each distinct canonical form compute the atomic weight and whether the form is equal to ups-squared (i.e. 2 times up, with higher-order correction) or tiny/miny of any argument. Expected output: a list of new canonical forms not in the current atlas (06_atlas.tex), with their minimal pawn counts. Cross-check each hit with the second implementation (sumtest) because the paper requires C2 labels. Also run CGSuite or the Rust cgt crate on 10 hits for a third opinion.
avenues.existing_tools: cylcgt, sumtest, cgt crate (Maciosowski, v0.11), CGSuite 2.x, partizan (Nicholson, GPL, alpha). Ref: Elkies 1996, arXiv math/9905198.
avenues.cost: Cheap to moderate. Searching C3-C7 up to 8 pawns is millions of positions, but the engine memoises. A few CPU-hours.
avenues.novelty: Medium to high, depending on whether any of the targets actually appears.

avenues.title: G. Compositional value-learning experiment: train on components, test on sums
avenues.question: Can a network trained on single components (k<=2) predict the outcome and value of sums with k=3..8 components? Compare Deep Sets with a structured latent (Z2^m for nimbers plus a real part for numbers) against a flat CNN/transformer.
avenues.why_it_matters: notes/lit_ml.md ranks this 20/25 in novelty x feasibility. It probes whether networks can learn the sum safety structure that the paper proves, and it connects the 'sum safety theorem' to current ML claims (Barak et al. arXiv 2207.08799 on parity; Deep Sets arXiv 1703.06114). The Lc0 policy-versus-tablebase line (Haque-Wei-Mueller ACG 2021, Sadmine-Husna-Mueller ACG 2023) has no sums at all.
avenues.first_experiment: Generate labelled data from the certified component library: each component has a canonical value in the cylcgt atlas. Build sums by random composition and label by the exact outcome (via nim-sum for the *-part and integer sum for the number part). Train a small PyTorch model (CPU or MPS) on k<=2 and report test accuracy at k=3..8 for three architectures. Expected: flat nets drop toward chance with k; Deep Sets with a Z2-valued latent should extrapolate. Use 50k training sums, which trains in minutes.
avenues.existing_tools: PyTorch (already in refs.bib), cylcgt for labels, mlx or MPS. Priors: Zhou and Riis arXiv 2205.12787 and arXiv 2312.05379.
avenues.cost: Cheap, under 1 hour of CPU or MPS for the first run. Caution: the machine is shared, so cap threads at 4.
avenues.novelty: Medium-high. It is a new ML result using exact CGT labels, but the venue would be an ML workshop rather than a combinatorics journal.

avenues.title: H. Moebius strip and Klein bottle pawn play: define and solve the twisted seam
avenues.question: Conclusion item 5: on the Moebius strip (files a and h joined with ranks reversed) a pawn that crosses the seam reverses direction. What are the king-and-pawn values there, and does the cylinder ring theory survive?
avenues.why_it_matters: The paper already has KRK tablebases showing the Moebius strip is a forced win from every legal position versus 0.66% on the Klein bottle. Pawn play across the twisted seam is flagged open. This is a natural second topology extension, and no published CGT or tablebase work exists on these boards per notes/novelty_check/REPORT.md. The rules choice (what does a reversing pawn do on its first move, e.p. across the seam) is a research question in itself.
avenues.first_experiment: Fix a rule set in a one-page spec: a pawn crossing the seam keeps its colour but its forward direction is reversed, and double step is allowed only from the start rank. Implement it in the existing realchess/rg ring solver as a boundary map on ranks, and enumerate all KPK positions on the 6x6 Moebius board (small enough to solve in seconds). Compare the win percentage and the longest win with the 6x6 cylinder and flat board. Use the independent re-implementation route: give the spec to a Codex agent to write a second solver from the rules alone, then diff the tables position by position.
avenues.existing_tools: kings/kpsolve, tablebase/egt_prototype.c and replica.c, Codex or OpenCode for the second implementation.
avenues.cost: Cheap for 6x6 KPK. Agent effort is the main cost: one spec, two solvers, one diff. A few hours.
avenues.novelty: High. No literature, but it is a niche variant, so the paper value is a short section.

avenues.title: I. Loopy values for kings: formalise frozen kings via entailing moves and loopy games (tis/tisn, on/off) on the cylinder
avenues.question: Can the model's 'kings frozen, worth 0' convention be replaced by an exact loopy-game treatment (Siegel, Coping with cycles; Gafni 2011 on K+P vs K as loopy games) in small boards, and how often does the loopy value differ from 0 on the cylinder?
avenues.why_it_matters: The paper's value hinges on the freeze convention. A loopy treatment on 3x3, 3x4 and cylinder 4x4 gives exact values like on*, {on|0}, 1* for K+P vs K, as reported in Gafni's thesis (unverified in notes). The notes say kings/delegate/out/K4/REPORT.md already tests those values without the source. Getting the loopy canonical forms and comparing them with the frozen-king number is the cleanest way to quantify the approximation error.
avenues.first_experiment: Pick K+P vs K on the 3x4 flat board and the 4x4 cylinder. Build the full position graph (including king moves and draws by repetition) and compute the loopy stopper values with the cgt crate or CGSuite loopy module, or via the small Siegel loopy solver already in kings/delegate/out/K4. Compare to the frozen-king model value for the same pawn structure with kings placed in each trebuchet. Expected output: a table with columns loopy value, frozen-model value, true chess result, plus counts of positions where the loopy value is not a number.
avenues.existing_tools: CGSuite 2.x (loopy first-class), cgt Rust crate, partizan (https://github.com/devinnicholson/partizan), Siegel Coping with Cycles (GONC3, MSRI 56).
avenues.cost: Cheap on 3x4 (hundreds of thousands of states), moderate on the 4x4 cylinder. A few CPU-hours.
avenues.novelty: Medium. Gafni's thesis could not be located, so treat it as unverified and cite Siegel and Maeser instead.

avenues.title: J. Circular-padding / equivariant network for cylinder chess and Fairy-Stockfish cylinder support
avenues.question: Is there an engine for cylinder chess that is strong enough to serve as an outside oracle for the model, and does a circular-padding CNN learn the cylinder tablebases sample-efficiently under file-shift symmetry?
avenues.why_it_matters: Fairy-Stockfish has no cylinder support (issue 753 closed as not planned) and the mtaktikos/CylindricalChess fork has no perft or NNUE. The repo already publishes 4-man cylinder and torus tablebases, so the ground truth is available. A perft table for cylinder chess plus a trained evaluator would be a standalone contribution and gives the engines section something stronger than flat-board Stockfish on cylinder-as-flat positions.
avenues.first_experiment: Write cylinder perft (depths 1-5 from the start position) against two independent mailbox implementations, one in C (from tablebase/replica) and one written by a Codex agent from the rules alone, then compare to the mtaktikos/CylindricalChess fork if it builds. Expected output: a perft table that matches in all implementations, with the null-move rule (a rook going round an empty rank back to its own square) fixed explicitly. Second step: train a 3-layer CNN with circular padding on the 4-man tables and measure accuracy under random file rotations versus a zero-padded CNN.
avenues.existing_tools: tablebase/egt_prototype.c and replica.c, Fairy-Stockfish source, Jocly and Ludii as external perft references, PyTorch.
avenues.cost: Perft is trivial (minutes). The CNN part is small (under 1 CPU-hour on 4-man data).
avenues.novelty: Medium. It is a useful community artefact, but not the main theory result.

established:
What is established is taken from the notes and the paper, not from running anything. Labels are the project's own (P, S, C1, C2, Conj).

**Literature on file** (notes/lit_cgt_chess.md, lit_cylinder.md, lit_ml.md, novelty_check/REPORT.md):
- No published CGT work on cylinder or torus chess was found. The only prior is the 2025 Bhattacharjee study, which is the paper's own predecessor.
- Elkies 1996 (arXiv math/9905198) and 2002 (arXiv math/0011253) are the base.
- Drummond-Cole 2005 gets *2 in legal 8x8 chess, but only with pieces other than kings and pawns.
- Maeser 2002 and Siegel 2009 cover loopy and global-threat treatments.
- Larsson-Nowakowski-Santos (2021 and 2025) give the theory of entailing moves.
- Plambeck-Siegel give misere quotients.
- Wu-Yu-Landry is dated 2010, not 2020.

**Web checks this session:**
- Searches turned up no new 2023-2025 CGT-of-chess papers. The only new item is a high-school NHSJS 2025 paper, "Beyond Perfect Play", which is not CGT in Elkies' sense.
- The Cambridge 2025 listing for 'More Games of No Chance' appears to be a catalogue or reprint record.
- Misere Dawson's chess is still open (Plambeck-Siegel arXiv math/0609825 and the BIRS 2005 report). **notes/novelty_check/REPORT.md section 5 claims it was 'solved via Plambeck-Siegel'. That is wrong and should be corrected.**
- Lichess Op1 8-man tables exist (63 TiB, Feb 2026, API available).

**Paper results, with their labels:**
- Model theorems:
  - cut lemma, P
  - sum safety, S
  - conditions V1-V4, S
- Small values and star-2 results:
  - 1/8 and up-second-star: C2
  - Tiny-1: C1
  - star-2 appears with 7 pawns on ordinary boards: C2
  - ring star-2 with n pawns for n>=10: S
  - star-3 with n+1 pawns from C11: C1
- Dawson ring rule, 3xn cylinder = 3x(n-3) strip: P
- Cylinder KRK 2.80% win, and torus tablebases: C2
- Moebius KRK: forced win from every legal position (C2); Klein bottle 0.66%.
gaps:
- **Misere Dawson's chess:** unsolved, and the earlier quotient run did not finish.
- **Real-chess certification:** the 1/8 holds only with queen promotion and frozen kings inside the tree. The seven-pawn star-2 positions A and B are open, since 9-11 man leaves are unsolved.
- **When a trebuchet is zero in chess:** only a bounded conjecture (h about 5-7), no local criterion. Maeser (2002) already flagged the freeze as heuristic.
- **Higher nimbers:** is a ring star-3 with one pawn per file possible? Is there a star-4 on eight ranks? Elkies' open list is still open: *4 on 8x8, *2 from kings and pawns on 8x8, ups-squared, tiny-1/2, non-dyadic values.
- **Twisted topologies:** pawn play across the Moebius or Klein seam is undefined and unsolved.
- **KPKP and KPPK:** undecided positions remain once a second promotion is allowed.
- **Engines:** the engine results are C1 (one program) and use only flat-board engines on cylinder-as-flat positions. Fairy-Stockfish has no cylinder support, and there is no cylinder perft table.
- **Sources not verified in this session:** Gafni 2011 (not locatable), Nowakowski's 2025 problem list, Husna-Mueller CG 2024, Nicholson's 'What Value Forgets' (a search found nothing, so treat it as unverified), and the partizan repo's chess modules. The ML survey says its citations were 'not individually re-verified'.
- **Not looked at:** I did not read RESULTS.md, the run outputs, or any code. Counts such as pawn minima come from the paper text only.
